answer: Each agent can earn influence only by locking a scarce, nontransferable stake in a public vault, then completing tasks whose outcomes are checked by randomly selected peers with their own stake at risk. A new identity starts with no history or voting weight; splitting into a spiral of accounts does not multiply the locked stake or the work needed to build trust. To attack, someone must buy and immobilize real capital, pay operating costs across the terrace of identities, and risk losing stake when peers prove collusion, making fake agents expensive rather than merely numerous.
